direction.comments: The direction on a macroscale is honestly a reason the movie isn't that great, as it looks so bland and boring and doesn't build its world well at all, and it feels even more amateurish coming out the year after Hamnet, an objectively better movie that I don't think was that great either; the direction on a microscale is good but not great, as it mostly lets the actors play, so the performances flow through Andrew Scott and you see the weight of the AIDS epidemic on these characters, and his scenes with Olivia Colman are a highlight even though they don't utilize that relationship well at all, yet for a movie that's supposed to be very emotional, it never evokes enough emotion to make me feel sad; the storytelling is good, mainly because it's such an interesting real-world story with a very good concept, and the fact that 1989 is now a period piece and Daniel Day-Lewis is treated as a historical figure gave me massive whiplash and made me feel so old; the tension is built decently well, since you're very attached to Ian and feel for him as the illness takes over, but it could have been better, as the movie doesn't know when to end and turns into a bunch of adrenaline dumps where you think your time with this character is over, only for it to keep going until you're begging it to end, so while there is tension, it's not held properly

performance.comments: Very good, as he transforms himself into the role and shows it all, from comedy, empathy, and anger to how sick the disease is making him, along with his drive and hunger to play Hamlet and go out on top with the role that defines him, and while he does a very good job with poor material, the director really held him back, so for this performance to be truly Oscar-worthy, he would have needed a new director; all the performances flow through him as he brings the best out of everyone, with good chemistry across the cast, especially Olivia Colman, as I enjoyed their scenes together even though the writing wasn't great, and pretty good chemistry with Billie Piper too

Does a good job with the not-great material she's given, but they very much underutilize her, as her relationship with Ian and the AIDS storyline should have been the crux of the movie instead of the Hamlet performance, since their banter and chemistry are probably the best parts of it, and she shows she's a good actress, so I wish I got to see more of her

To be real, I watched this whole movie without realizing this was Billie Piper, which shocked me since I really like her, and she gives a pretty good performance, and her good chemistry with Andrew Scott makes their dynamic pretty fun

cast.comments: Mostly characters meant to support Andrew Scott, and they know their job and do it well

story.comments: The concept is a really cool one, as it follows the final role of Ian Charleson's career, where he gives one of the most powerful performances of Hamlet while battling AIDS and keeping it hidden from the world as he tries to stay alive and gives it his all; the plot structure is linear, and while the first hour is structured well, the climax and resolution in the last 50 minutes go on for way too long, so it feels very bloated, and cutting about half of that would have made this an hour and a half instead of an hour and 50 minutes; character writing is good for Ian Charleson, as you care about him and see him suffer both mentally and physically while still wanting this performance of Hamlet to be the last thing he gives the world and to redefine his career so he's not just the guy from Chariots of Fire, but everyone else is bland, generic, and surface level, so you don't really care about anybody else or their relationships with him, as his scenes with his best friend aren't written that well, and even though I liked Olivia Colman's performance, their relationship isn't given enough to make you care

screenplay.comments: The dialogue is good for the most part, though it has some issues, like spamming the 'to be or not to be' joke way too many times, with three in the first 30 minutes alone, which got very annoying, because we get it: this is a movie about Hamlet; the humor is decent, with enough of it to make a very emotional movie feel somewhat lighthearted; the symbolism shows Ian's perseverance and triumphant nature as he gets this performance of Hamlet across amid everything he's going through, but it never made me feel sad, even at the end, unlike other emotional movies I've seen this year, which comes down to the bland character writing and microscale direction; the foreshadowing is definitely there even though everybody knows how this movie ends, as it plants roots that make the ending somewhat relevant, but it feels the need to uproot every one of them, which drags the ending out longer than it needs to be

score.comments: Well composed, and I did enjoy it, but it feels overbearing and poorly mixed into the movie, especially at the end, where it's way too loud, so it ends up feeling kind of forced

cinematography.comments: So dull and bland, with undersaturated colors that make the movie even more boring to look at, along with a lot of amateurish shots, including shaky ones that made me feel nauseated, so it feels like a very poorly shot movie, as if an amateur made it

editing.comments: Spliced together so choppily, with way too many cuts, badly edited montages, and awkwardly stitched shots, like in the argument sequence at the brick wall, which is so poorly executed from a direction, cinematography, and editing perspective, and the cut is genuinely too long, as you could have trimmed about 25 minutes from the last 50

sound.comments: Fine and what you'd expect from a movie of this scale

production_design.comments: Set in late-1980s London, and while I did enjoy them shooting at the National Theatre and the rehearsal sets are kind of cool too, overall it's a very generic production design

makeup.comments: Plays an important role in showing the blotches and how sick the characters are getting from AIDS, which is a key storytelling element, and they do a pretty good job with it

costumes.comments: Good, as they're very much theatrical Hamlet costumes, and while they're not the best, I enjoyed them

review.pacing: Fine for the first hour, but the rest is poorly paced and goes on for way too long, as they just didn't know when to end this movie, so while they could keep the first half the same, they should have cut 20 to 25 minutes from the second half
review.climax: Very bland and anticlimactic, especially since it's literally the same climax as Hamnet, with them performing Hamlet and how it affects the characters, except Hamnet's is shot so well that it's one of the best climaxes I've seen, while this one feels shoehorned in, very forced, and drags on far too long
review.tone: A very generic, boring, and bland drama biopic about a theater actor
review.final_notes: Saw it as the closing night film at Austin Film Festival
review.overall: Overall, while Andrew Scott delivers a borderline Oscar-worthy performance and the concept is very interesting, 'Elsinore' is just not a well-made movie, as it's poorly executed and put together, from its dull, undersaturated cinematography and choppy editing to a movie that doesn't know when to end
